# HeaderMenuInteractionNL's motion check races drag speed against its fixed window

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderMenuInteractionNL.spec.mjs:356` failed on hosted CI after #20455 (#20454's fix). The run was #20479's e2e-engine shard 5, run [42282441953](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42282441953). It failed only this assertion; 61 tests passed.

```text
expect(observed.samples.some(sample => sample.rects[0]?.width > box.width + 40)).toBe(true)
Expected: true
Received: false
```

The trace keeps the receipt the test attaches before asserting (`header-resize-motion`). The window opened at the gesture, as #20455 intended, and the header grew live under the held pointer. The width read 150 px at 0 ms, then 160 at 295 ms, 175 at 1034 ms, 186 at 1591 ms and 190 at 1738 ms, which was the last sample in the 1800 ms window. The runner was slow: 26 samples where a 32 ms interval gives about 56. The +65 px, 30-step drag had reached exactly `box.width + 40` when the window closed, and the assertion needs strictly more. Every other assertion passed, including the held-pointer DOM poll for `> box.width + 40`.

## The Problem

The assertion asks for a target magnitude inside a fixed wall-clock window, while the input that produces it takes runner-dependent time. #20454 moved the window's start to the gesture, which removed the hover wait. It could not remove the dependence on how fast the drag progresses.

## The Architectural Reality

- Lines 330–357: `mouse.down`, then `observeMotion({durationMs: 1800, intervalMs: 32})`, then a 30-step `mouse.move`. Next comes a held-pointer `expect.poll` of the header's bounding box `> box.width + 40`, then `mouse.up`. After the drop, a component-width poll checks `> box.width + 40`, and finally the motion assertion runs.
- The target size is therefore already asserted twice without a clock: during the hold, and after the drop. What only the motion receipt can show is that the width grows live, frame by frame, while the pointer is held, rather than jumping at the drop.

## The Fix

Replace the magnitude-in-window check with the receipt's own claim: the sampled width rises in at least two steps (at least three increasing values, so live growth, never one jump at the drop), and its maximum exceeds `box.width`. A "never shrinks" rule is deliberately left out, because a one-pixel snap at the drop would trip it without saying anything about live resize. The window's placement and length stay as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The motion assertion checks live growth (at least two rises in the sampled width, maximum above the start), not `> box.width + 40` inside the window.
- [ ] The CI receipt from run 42282441953 satisfies the new check. A synthetic receipt that stays flat and then jumps once fails it.
- [ ] `durationMs` is unchanged, and the held-pointer and post-drop `> box.width + 40` polls are unchanged.
- [ ] The spec passes locally through the off-socket engine tier.

## Out of Scope

- `observeMotion`'s fixed-window contract (#20454's Out of Scope stands).
- Motion assertions in other specs.

## Avoided Traps

- Raising `durationMs`: #20454 already rejected it, because it moves the bet and keeps the race.
- Lowering the +40 threshold: the race remains, at a different number.
